claims.text: The starting W38Ta36Cr15V11 alloy has a uniform nanocrystalline grain structure.
Introducing no more than 0.5 at.% Y by pre-alloying and oxidizing annealing at about 800°C for 1–2 hours will form fine Y2O3 nanoparticles.
The in situ Y2O3 nanoparticles will preferentially decorate grain boundaries.
The Y2O3 nanoparticles will be well dispersed.
Grain-boundary Y2O3 nanoparticles will act as efficient sinks for radiation-induced point defects.
The Y2O3 nanoparticles will trap mobile Cr and V solute atoms.
Trapping radiation-induced defects and Cr/V solutes will impede nucleation and growth of irradiation-induced Cr/V precipitates.
The intervention will reduce irradiation-induced Cr/V precipitation by more than 70% relative to unmodified W38Ta36Cr15V11 after irradiation near 500°C to approximately 8 dpa.
Irradiation hardening in the modified alloy will remain within 5% of that in the unmodified alloy.
Controlled oxidation and precise annealing will prevent the Y addition from compromising the nanocrystalline structure responsible for minimal irradiation hardening.
The modified microstructure will remain homogeneous after irradiation.
The intervention will improve the alloy's suitability for practical bulk fabrication.
Unmodified nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 will exhibit significant Cr/V precipitation after irradiation at 500°C to approximately 8 dpa.
Unmodified nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 will retain low irradiation hardening under the specified irradiation conditions.
The proposed intervention is effective near 500°C and up to approximately 8 dpa.
Maintaining the annealing temperature near 800°C under a controlled oxidizing atmosphere will avoid excessive oxide coarsening and grain growth.
